what_it_does: Federated learning is a way to train an AI model across many devices (such as smart home sensors or wearables) without sending raw data to a central server — each device trains locally and only shares model updates. In a decentralized version, devices also do not talk to a single central coordinator; instead they communicate directly with each other. The problem is that small IoT devices have very limited computing power and wireless bandwidth, and the data on each device looks very different from device to device (called non-IID, meaning not identically distributed). MMDFL sends multiple lightweight model copies (called traveler models) on a circuit around the network, so each model sees data from many devices without requiring every device to exchange updates with every neighbor simultaneously. Which devices each traveler visits is chosen adaptively based on data diversity and available resources, reducing wasted communication.
